name: Seleucid Empire (Antiochus III)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 3.6 million km2 for 312-201 BCE (high) and a declining range of 2.3 million to 475,000 km2 for 200-147 BCE (mid = start of that range). The historical-basemaps world_bc200 polygon measures 1.75 million km2 on the sphere (computed from the GeoJSON, low); it omits Coele-Syria (taken at Panium in 200) and the tributary upper satrapies.

population.note: Seshat codes two disputed values for 312-63 BCE: 16 million and 30 million. In 200 the empire had lost nothing yet to Rome and had just regained Coele-Syria (Panium), but the upper satrapies (Bactria, Parthia) were only tributary after the anabasis of 212-205; low 14 million allows for their exclusion, high 30 million is the larger Seshat value. Everything inside the border; Bactria and Parthia (vassal kings) not counted in the mid.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Seshat (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/108) codes the largest settlement at 50,000-100,000 for 312-63 BCE (Antioch, Seleucia on the Tigris). Dense Greek city foundations in Syria and Babylonia, rural plateau; scaled below Roman 117 CE (10-25%).

activePersonnel.note: Royal field army (49,500 / 66,000 / 89,000, see forces) + fleet crews, mahouts, engineers and staff (15,000 / 28,000 / 40,000, see supportPersonnel) + city and fortress garrisons from Sardis to Susa (20,000 / 30,000 / 50,000; educated guess). Convention: the royal army, guards and garrisons under arms are counted as active; military settlers (katoikoi) and vassal contingents not called up are in trainedReserves.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Military settlers (katoikoi) of Syria, Mesopotamia, Media and Lydia not called up for Panium, plus vassal contingents (Bactria, Armenia, Cappadocia) callable within weeks; Bar-Kochva (isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2) treats the settlers as the phalanx reserve. audit 2026-10-30: ISBN corrected from 9780521200745 (resolves to The Agrarian History of England and Wales) to 9780521206679 (Bar-Kochva, The Seleucid Army, Open Library work OL2927924W) throughout this file.

supportPersonnel.note: Fleet: decked ships (40 / 70 / 100) x ~250 crew + lighter craft (100 / 150 / 200) x ~50; plus ~2-3 mahouts and attendants per elephant and ~2,000-4,000 engineers, staff and royal pages.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Maximum field armies (~70,000) plus garrisons were ~0.5% of the population; the Macedonian-armed core depended on a limited pool of military settlers (Bar-Kochva, isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2). Total-war ratio assumes wide levying of native and allied contingents.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Three documented field armies bracket the 200 BCE royal army: Raphia 217 (Polybius 5.79, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): 62,000 foot, 6,000 horse, 102 elephants; Magnesia 190 (Livy 37.40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37): phalanx 16,000, 6,000 cataphracts, agema 1,000, royal cavalry 1,000, 54 elephants, ~70,000 in all; Daphne parade 166 (Polybius 30.25, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/30*.html): 20,000 Macedonian-armed, 5,000 Roman-armed, ~20,000 allies and mercenaries, ~8,500 cavalry. Bar-Kochva, The Seleucid Army (isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2-3 and the battle chapters) accepts these figures as broadly reliable musters of the royal army (ancient figures, hence grade C). Line infantry = Macedonian-armed phalanx (16,000-20,000) + argyraspides guard (~10,000 picked men in Macedonian arms, Polybius 5.79.4) + Greek and Galatian mercenary heavy infantry (3,000-10,000).

quality.note: Sarissa phalanx and silver-shield guard: era-typical to among the era's best (rubric 0.75); mercenaries era-typical.

training.note: Argyraspides a standing guard (0.75); phalanx of settler-reservists called up for campaigns (0.5-0.75). Polybius 5.66 says the army was not exercised in winter 218/217.

count.note: Three documented field armies bracket the 200 BCE royal army: Raphia 217 (Polybius 5.79, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): 62,000 foot, 6,000 horse, 102 elephants; Magnesia 190 (Livy 37.40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37): phalanx 16,000, 6,000 cataphracts, agema 1,000, royal cavalry 1,000, 54 elephants, ~70,000 in all; Daphne parade 166 (Polybius 30.25, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/30*.html): 20,000 Macedonian-armed, 5,000 Roman-armed, ~20,000 allies and mercenaries, ~8,500 cavalry. Bar-Kochva, The Seleucid Army (isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2-3 and the battle chapters) accepts these figures as broadly reliable musters of the royal army (ancient figures, hence grade C). Light infantry = Arab, Median, Cissian, Carmanian, Cilician, Thracian and Pisidian javelinmen and peltasts (Raphia ~23,000, Magnesia ~12,000).

quality.note: Ethnic light equipment, era-typical to below (rubric 0.25-0.5).

count.note: Three documented field armies bracket the 200 BCE royal army: Raphia 217 (Polybius 5.79, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): 62,000 foot, 6,000 horse, 102 elephants; Magnesia 190 (Livy 37.40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37): phalanx 16,000, 6,000 cataphracts, agema 1,000, royal cavalry 1,000, 54 elephants, ~70,000 in all; Daphne parade 166 (Polybius 30.25, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/30*.html): 20,000 Macedonian-armed, 5,000 Roman-armed, ~20,000 allies and mercenaries, ~8,500 cavalry. Bar-Kochva, The Seleucid Army (isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2-3 and the battle chapters) accepts these figures as broadly reliable musters of the royal army (ancient figures, hence grade C). Missile infantry = Cretan and Neocretan archers (2,500 at Raphia, ~2,500 at Magnesia), Persian and Agrianian bowmen and slingers (2,000 at Raphia), Mysian bowmen (2,500 at Magnesia), Cyrtian slingers and Elymaean archers.

quality.note: Cretan archers renowned; Iranian composite bows (rubric 0.5-0.75).

count.note: Three documented field armies bracket the 200 BCE royal army: Raphia 217 (Polybius 5.79, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): 62,000 foot, 6,000 horse, 102 elephants; Magnesia 190 (Livy 37.40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37): phalanx 16,000, 6,000 cataphracts, agema 1,000, royal cavalry 1,000, 54 elephants, ~70,000 in all; Daphne parade 166 (Polybius 30.25, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/30*.html): 20,000 Macedonian-armed, 5,000 Roman-armed, ~20,000 allies and mercenaries, ~8,500 cavalry. Bar-Kochva, The Seleucid Army (isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2-3 and the battle chapters) accepts these figures as broadly reliable musters of the royal army (ancient figures, hence grade C). Heavy cavalry = Companions and agema (1,000 each) + cataphracts, first attested for the Seleucids at Panium 200 (Polybius 16.18.6-8, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/16*.html: the "mailed horsemen" of the younger Antiochus) and 6,000 strong at Magnesia.

quality.note: Fully armoured cataphracts on armoured horses and the guard cavalry; the era's best heavy cavalry (rubric 1.0). Panium was won by the cataphract charge.

training.note: Guard units professional (0.75-1.0); cataphracts newly raised after the anabasis.

count.note: Three documented field armies bracket the 200 BCE royal army: Raphia 217 (Polybius 5.79, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/5*.html): 62,000 foot, 6,000 horse, 102 elephants; Magnesia 190 (Livy 37.40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37): phalanx 16,000, 6,000 cataphracts, agema 1,000, royal cavalry 1,000, 54 elephants, ~70,000 in all; Daphne parade 166 (Polybius 30.25, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/30*.html): 20,000 Macedonian-armed, 5,000 Roman-armed, ~20,000 allies and mercenaries, ~8,500 cavalry. Bar-Kochva, The Seleucid Army (isbn:9780521206679, ch. 2-3 and the battle chapters) accepts these figures as broadly reliable musters of the royal army (ancient figures, hence grade C). Light cavalry = Tarentines (at Panium, Polybius 16.18.7), Dahae horse archers (1,200 at Magnesia), Galatian horse, Arab camel archers.

quality.note: Horse archers and javelin cavalry, era-typical to good.

count.note: Polybius 11.34.12 (https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Polybius/11*.html): after the anabasis (206) Antiochus' elephants "amounted now to a hundred and fifty" (high). Raphia 217: 102 (Polybius 5.79.13); Magnesia 190: 54 (Livy 37.39-40, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_37, low end allows for this decline). Elephants were used at Panium (Polybius 16.18.7). Indian elephants. Mahouts in supportPersonnel.

quality.note: Indian elephants with towers, larger than the African forest elephants of the Ptolemies (Polybius 5.84, Livy 37.39); among the era's best (rubric 0.75-1.0).

training.note: Professional Indian mahouts; elephants stabled and trained at Apamea.

count.note: Livy 33.19 (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_33): in spring 197 Antiochus sailed with "a hundred decked ships and two hundred smaller vessels" after calling up "the whole strength of his kingdom" (high). Livy 37 (https://www.gutenberg.org/files/44318/44318-h/44318-h.htm, Polyxenidas 190): seventy decked ships (mid). Low allows for ships not yet built in 200. Quadriremes, quinqueremes and a few larger polyremes (Livy 37.23-24, Side 190).

quality.note: Era-typical to good Hellenistic polyremes, Phoenician-built; defeated by the Rhodians and Romans in 190.

training.note: Phoenician crews; less experienced than the Rhodian navy.

count.note: Livy 33.19 (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/From_the_Founding_of_the_City/Book_33): 200 smaller vessels "including swift pinnaces and Cyprian barques" in 197 (high); mid and low allow for the 200 BCE fleet being smaller.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: Antiochus III "the Great", proven by the anabasis (212-205) and the cavalry victory at Panium; but he lost Raphia (217) by an over-long pursuit, and the officer corps was court-based rather than a trained staff.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: Macedonian-armed core with strong identity (0.75), large allied and subject contingents (0.25).

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: motivated, recent victories (anabasis, Panium 200, conquest of Coele-Syria).

weapons.note: Anchor 3 (300 BCE: iron weapons, torsion artillery, sarissa) plus war elephants and cataphract lances.

armor.note: Anchor 3 (bronze/iron cuirass, mail) plus full cataphract armour for horse and rider; still well short of anchor 4 plate-and-mail. audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.2 -> 3.06, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -200 (3.065); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

ships.note: Anchor 3 (triremes, quinqueremes) with larger polyremes (hepteres at Side 190). audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.2 -> 3.06, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -200 (3.065); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

fortification.note: Anchor 3: ashlar city walls and citadels (Antioch, Apamea, Dura-Europos); siege trains reduced Sardis (214) and Bactra (208-206).

logistics.note: Anchor 3: inherited Achaemenid road and depot system, royal granaries; the anabasis marched to Bactria and India and back.

communications.note: Anchor 3: mounted relay posts on the former Achaemenid royal roads.

isr.note: Year anchor 3: mounted scouts and Tarentine light horse.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: year 1 CE values for Iraq, Iran, Israel and Jordan 1,116, Turkey 897 (2011 int$). Applied two centuries earlier to a Syria-Mesopotamia-Iran core; western Iran and Anatolian holdings poorer.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Standing guard, mercenaries, elephants and fleet paid in coin from a royal revenue Livy and Polybius describe as vast; the military-settler phalanx was paid largely in land. Similar order to Ptolemaic Egypt (army and navy ~34% of the royal budget per Fischer-Bovet).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Agrarian empire with craft centres in Syria, Phoenicia and Babylonia.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Irrigated Mesopotamian agriculture and the Syrian plains produced large surpluses (Seleucia on the Tigris supplied by Babylonian grain).

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Inherited Achaemenid royal roads (Sardis-Susa ~2,500 km and branches to Ecbatana, Bactra, Persepolis) plus Syrian routes; no engineered network on the Roman scale. Same order as persia-achaemenid--480.

majorPorts.note: Seleucia Pieria, Laodicea-on-Sea, Tyre, Sidon, Ptolemais-Akko (taken 200) and the Cilician ports; Ephesus only from 197. Count by analogy with persia-achaemenid--480.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Phoenician and Cilician merchant shipping; below the Achaemenid total since Egypt and the Aegean are outside the empire.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pack-animal and wagon-supplied Hellenistic armies operated about one to two weeks' march from a depot or navigable river; elephants added large fodder needs.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.07 / 0.09 / 0.11 draft and pack animals (oxen, mules, camels, horses) per inhabitant x population.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: familiar terrain, local supply and fortified Greek cities in Syria and Mesopotamia; native and Iranian loyalty weaker, so below 1.2 mid.

notes: Snapshot = late 200 BCE, Antiochus III after Panium, at the height of his reconquests. Forces are the royal field army at Raphia/Panium/Magnesia scale (Bar-Kochva treats these musters as the effective maximum of the Seleucid army); garrisons are only in activePersonnel. Ancient figures (Polybius, Livy) used for composition and as bounds, graded C. Scythed chariots (Magnesia 190) and the siege train are not counted: no number survives for 200. Bactria (Euthydemus) and Parthia (Arsaces II) were vassal kingdoms after the anabasis; inside the Seshat extent but not counted in the mid population. Population convention: Seshat range.
